executiveSummary.headline: Earnings resilience steadies stocks as inflation and tech upheaval jolt yields & crypto
executiveSummary.body: Global risk assets staged a choppy rebound last week as strong Q3 corporate earnings outweighed renewed inflation anxiety and major leadership upheaval in megacap tech. Higher-than-expected US inflation pushed Treasury yields back up and triggered a sharp crypto sell-off, while oil eased off October highs despite Middle East geopolitical risk.

marketsMacro.title: Global Equities & Indices
marketsMacro.summary: US stocks rebounded despite Nvidia’s ~13% drop on leadership upheaval, buoyed by 32% YoY Q3 earnings growth.
bullets: Nvidia fell ~13% (erasing $500B in market value) after Jensen Huang’s resignation and CFO Colette Kress becoming interim CEO.
Despite Nvidia’s slide, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) still rallied ~8% on rotation into peers.
Q3 S&P 500 earnings are tracking ~32% YoY, with all 11 sectors on pace for positive full-year growth.
European and UK equities showed lower volatility than US peers given smaller megacap AI concentration.

marketsMacro.title: Macroeconomics & Central Banks
marketsMacro.summary: Hotter US inflation keeps a December Fed hike in play as the BoE and RBA tighten policy further.
bullets: US Oct Core CPI rose +0.3% MoM (above 0.2% consensus) alongside firmer PPI, keeping a December Fed hike firmly in focus.
UK markets are digesting the BoE’s 25 bps hike to 4.00% (8–1 vote, Catherine Mann dissenting for 50 bps) ahead of the 17 Dec meeting.
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) hiked 25 bps to 4.85%.
Ongoing Iran conflict continues to keep global supply-chain pressures elevated.

marketsMacro.title: Fixed Income & Credit
marketsMacro.summary: A four-week Treasury rally reversed on sticky US inflation, while corporate credit held firm.
bullets: Hotter US inflation reversed a 4-week Treasury rally, pushing the 10-year yield back above 5.10%.
Corporate credit remained resilient despite heavy new issuance from tech and AI-linked borrowers.
Investment-grade (IG) and high-yield (HY) spreads stayed contained, with higher-quality issuers outperforming.

marketsMacro.title: Commodities & Energy
marketsMacro.summary: Crude eased off October highs while elevated diesel spreads and higher real yields shaped metals.
bullets: Crude cooled from October’s ~$108/bbl highs to mid-$90s Brent and ~$87 WTI.
Diesel crack spreads remain historically elevated, feeding through into freight and goods inflation.
Gold eased toward ~$3,900/oz as higher real yields pressured non-yielding bullion.

marketsMacro.title: Crypto & Digital Assets
marketsMacro.summary: Bitcoin broke below $70k amid institutional outflows and a record stablecoin supply contraction.
bullets: Sharp drawdown saw BTC break $70k down to $64k–$66k, while ETH slipped to ~$1,800.
Selling was driven by institutional outflows and renewed Federal Reserve tightening fears.
Coinbase Institutional reported a record $11.5B 30-day contraction in combined USDT, USDC, and DAI supply.

marketsMacro.title: Financial Regulation & Policy
marketsMacro.summary: Major UK PRA capital updates, FCA resilience & pension reviews, and EU-UK supervisory coordination.

subTabs.label: UK PRA
items: Published Large Exposures Framework (Part 2) Policy Statement.
Consolidates non-core large exposures group (NCLEG) permissions into a single permission.
Introduces a firm-specific higher trading-book limit of 350% of Tier 1 capital (up from 250% originally consulted).

subTabs.label: UK FCA
items: Released multi-firm review on operational resilience for trading venues ahead of March 2027 incident-reporting rules.
Opened CP26/40 consultation on exempting performance fees from the workplace pensions charge cap.

subTabs.label: UK-EU & Global
items: UK Financial Services and Markets Bill passed Second Reading in the House of Commons (10 Nov).
Joint EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum met on 11 Nov to coordinate cross-border supervision.
Basel Committee (BCBS) opened consultation on Pillar 2 IRRBB guidance.
EU adopted delegated regulations tightening ESG & transparency in credit rating methodologies.

sectors.name: Technology & AI
sectors.note: Nvidia -13% on leadership news vs. SOX +8% rotation into non-Nvidia chipmakers.

sectors.name: Banking & Financial Services
sectors.note: Outperformed in UK/Europe on higher-for-longer NIM support; Standard Chartered posted a +46% profit jump.

sectors.name: Energy & Oil/Gas
sectors.note: Top 2026 performer on elevated crude and refining margins, pausing near-term as Brent eased from $100+.

sectors.name: Healthcare & Biotech
sectors.note: Acted as a defensive ballast during tech volatility, drawing strong institutional flows.

sectors.name: Industrials & Defence
sectors.note: Profit-taking in European defence; US industrial capex remains supported by power and data-centre demand.

sectors.name: Consumer & Retail
sectors.note: Hit by sticky inflation and high rates; UK BRC retail sales grew just +1.1% YoY in Oct, with staples beating discretionary.

sectors.name: Real Estate & Infrastructure
sectors.note: Rate-sensitive property pressured by 5%+ US 10Y and 4.00% BoE (UK Lloyds HPI -0.6% MoM in Oct), while digital/power infra thrives (Anthropic $3.4B gas-powered data centre deal).

weekAhead.title: Nvidia Q3 Earnings
weekAhead.details: Focus on data-centre demand, gross margins, and interim CEO Colette Kress’s commentary on leadership continuity & hyperscaler capex.

weekAhead.title: Anthropic IPO (Pricing 18 Nov, Trading 19 Nov)
weekAhead.details: Reportedly ~6x oversubscribed at a $1.3T–$1.4T valuation; defining gauge for AI valuations and global capital markets appetite.

weekAhead.title: UK & APAC Macro Data
weekAhead.details: Watch UK wage/earnings data (BoE Dec rate path), RBA minutes, Australian Q3 wage & jobs, India Oct CPI (forecast 12.1% on food/fuel), and Bank Indonesia rate decision (expected +25 bps to 6.0%).
